== Biography ==
'''Nancy Glasgow''' was born about 1848 in County Antrim, Ireland. She was the daughter of [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann (McCracken) Glasgow]].

=== Early Life ===

Nancy was recorded with her family at Lisnagaver in the civil parish of Rasharkin, County Antrim, in the surviving 1851 census.

She was aged '''3''', giving an estimated birth year of about 1847 or 1848.

The household included:

* [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]], aged 35, farmer;
* [[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann (McCracken) Glasgow]], aged 29, wife;
* Rose Ann Glasgow, aged 10;
* Eliza Glasgow, aged 7;
* Jane Glasgow, aged 5;
* '''Nancy Glasgow''', aged 3;
* Margaret Glasgow, aged 1;
* Catherine McLaughlin, aged 15, servant.

<ref name="Census1851">National Archives of Ireland, ''Census of Ireland, 1851'', Lisnagaver, Rasharkin, County Antrim, household 37, Thomas Glasgow household; [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/37/ household return].</ref>

Nancy's parents and siblings formed part of a closely associated Glasgow family network at Lisnagaver. Her father Thomas was a farmer and a probable close relative, possibly a brother, of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]], who occupied the nearby household 35.

No surviving record presently proves the exact relationship between Thomas and Alexander.

=== Marriage ===

Nancy married [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]].

A secondary civil-registration index reports the marriage in the '''Ballymoney registration district''' during the first quarter of '''1879'''. Nancy was indexed as '''Nancy Glasgow''' and Robert's surname appears in the variants '''M‘Caughron''' and '''M‘Caughern'''.<ref name="Marriage1879">[https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 "Trying to find Glasgow", Genes Reunited], discussion quoting the civil-registration index: Nancy Glasgow, Ballymoney registration district, January–March 1879, vol. 1, p. 181, spouse Robert M‘Caughron/M‘Caughern (accessed 9 August 2026). This is a secondary transcription; the original civil marriage registration should be obtained.</ref>

This marriage is particularly relevant to the wider Glasgow family network.

Nancy's father [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] was married to [[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann McCracken]], while Thomas's probable close relative [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] was married to [[McCaughan-222|Mary "Molly" McCaughan]].

Nancy's own marriage to Robert McCaughen therefore provides another direct connection between the Glasgow and McCaughen families in the wider County Antrim network.

The relationship, if any, between [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]] and [[McCaughan-222|Mary McCaughan]] has not yet been established.

=== New Zealand ===

Nancy is reported to have later lived in New Zealand.

A burial on '''22 September 1937''' at '''Linwood Cemetery, Christchurch, Canterbury, New Zealand''' has been attributed to her.

The original cemetery or death record supporting this identification has not yet been added to this profile. Until it is obtained, the burial should be treated as provisional rather than as a proved life event.
A marriage for Annie Glasgow and McCaughern was registered on 14 May 1879 in the Coleraine district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 14 May 1879, Coleraine district, M/1879/K1/1048/4/75.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-987]] is assessed at 98% (proved). The held 1851 Lisnagaver account explicitly records this daughter of Thomas in the Mary Ann household. The proved baptisms of older siblings and coherent age sequence corroborate this specific father, independently of later marriages or death candidates.

Confidence concerns this recorded child and the selected father as identified by the held family evidence; maternity and the father’s upstream ancestry are separate.

Next useful test: Inspect the full 1851 relationship column and seek the child’s baptism in MIC1P/292.

Source basis already held: [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/37/ 1851 Ireland Census, residents of house 37, Lisnagaver, Rasharkin, Kilconway, County Antrim, National Archives of Ireland, household return (http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/37/) (accessed 12 May 2025).]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



=== Name ===

Nancy is recorded as '''Nancy Glasgow''' in the 1851 census and in the secondary index of her 1879 marriage.

A FamilySearch collaborative-tree entry associated with this family uses the name '''Annie Glasgow'''.<ref name="FamilySearch">FamilySearch Family Tree, database, entry for Annie Glasgow, PID [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/MQ57-1NV MQ57-1NV]. FamilySearch Family Tree is user-contributed and should not be treated as an original genealogical source.</ref>

Nancy can historically occur as a familiar form associated with Ann or Anne, but the FamilySearch naming should not by itself be used to change her documented name from Nancy.

=== McCracken and McCaughen ===

Nancy's mother is recorded as [[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann McCracken]].

The surname '''McCracken''' should not presently be treated as a transcription variant of '''McCaughen/McAughern'''.

The Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription repeatedly distinguishes the two surnames within the same register. Thomas Glasgow's wife appears as Mary Ann McCrackin or McCracken, while [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]]'s wife appears as Mary or Molly McAughin/McAughern.

Inspection of the original Rasharkin Presbyterian register, PRONI '''MIC.1P/292''', remains desirable before treating any particular spelling as definitive.

=== Glasgow–McCaughen Network ===

Nancy's marriage is significant because several links connect the two surname groups:

* Nancy was the daughter of [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]];
* Nancy married [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]];
* Thomas's probable close relative [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] married [[McCaughan-222|Mary "Molly" McCaughan]];
* Alexander and Thomas lived in the same small Lisnagaver community;
* Alexander and Thomas later occupied consecutive valuation lots 25 and 26 under the same landlord.

These facts support a close local FAN network.

They do '''not''' yet establish that Robert McCaughen and Mary McCaughan were siblings or otherwise closely related.

=== Thomas and Alexander Glasgow ===

[[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] were both County Antrim farmers associated with the same small Lisnagaver–Gortereagh–Moneyleck area.

They used the same Rasharkin Presbyterian congregation, headed closely grouped households in the surviving 1851 census, and later occupied consecutive valuation lots.

Their children also appear close together in the Rasharkin Presbyterian register. Alexander's son James was born at Lisnagaver on 9 October 1843, while Thomas's daughter Eliza was born there eight days later on 17 October 1843.

This provides substantial circumstantial evidence for a close relationship.

No surviving record presently calls Thomas and Alexander brothers. Thomas should therefore be treated as Alexander's '''probable close relative and possible brother''', not as a proved sibling.

=== Burial and Death ===

The reported burial date of '''22 September 1937''' at Linwood Cemetery requires verification.

Priority evidence would be:

* the Christchurch cemetery interment entry;
* a New Zealand civil death registration;
* probate or administration;
* a newspaper death notice or obituary;
* passenger or immigration evidence connecting Nancy and Robert to New Zealand.

The burial should not be treated as proved solely from a collaborative FamilySearch tree.

=== Priority Research ===

* Obtain the original 1879 civil marriage registration for Nancy Glasgow and [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]].
* Record Nancy's residence, age, occupation and father's name and occupation.
* Record Robert's residence, age, occupation, father and father's occupation.
* Record the church, minister and both witnesses.
* Establish Robert McCaughen's parents and siblings.
* Investigate whether Robert was related to [[McCaughan-222|Mary "Molly" McCaughan]], wife of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]].
* Verify Nancy and Robert's migration to New Zealand.
* Obtain the original New Zealand death and Linwood Cemetery records.
* Search New Zealand records under McCaughen, McCaughern, McCaughan and related spelling variants.
